analysis:
Docs-only PR: docs/architecture/inference.md (new load-time shape-warmup section, head ~956-1003; units 12/13 are unchanged surrounding text from line 1643 onward) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (new row at head line 1751 documenting DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP: `0` disables warmup, `always` skips its shader-cache probe). No code, wire, key, attestation, or cache-storage changes are visible, so no control regression is demonstrable.

Security-relevant observations, none a finding:
- The warmup is described as running synthetic prompts at load time with default sampling. It trains no rate or counter, shares a 20-second wall budget, and a timeout or refusal completes the attempt. Only the documentation is in this diff; the implementation (ModelCalibrationPolicy, EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibration) is not supplied.
- Open questions for later passes: whether warmup prompts or KV state can be donated to the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041) or the resident cache, and whether synthetic prompts could create cacheSalt-scoped entries or TTFT-oracle artifacts. The doc says nothing either way. Also whether warmup rows can contend with real consumer requests (availability, T-010/T-029) and whether the warmup delays the connection control or App Attest dispatch (TB-011). The text says preemption leaves it due, which suggests foreground priority.
- The new env var is a local operator-controlled knob. The operator is already in the TB-003 threat model with full local control, so this adds no new privilege.
- The warmup is a timing-only side effect with no consumer plaintext (A-001), so it does not touch the existing assets. The remaining unknown is the unseen implementation's cache interaction, so a low-priority follow-up is warranted but not a finding.
- The report link and shape-warmup details in the head excerpt are truncated at `Each finished pass reco...`; the rest is unverified.
